title: an inferred-fallible callback reaching a consumer as an array-literal element of an argument must spell a Result contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Inference and Public Contracts': 'Public, abstract, ambient, and declaration-only contracts MUST express fallibility directly with `Result<A, E>` or `Promise<Result<A, E>>`.' A callback boundary is a VALUE edge, not an argument position: the callee invokes a function it received inside an object literal, an array literal, a parenthesis, a cast or a `new` argument list exactly as it invokes one passed directly. Fail-closed matters here because the accepting behaviour is silent and wrong rather than loud and wrong — R1FIX executed this class before the fix and measured `isOk() === true` with a `Result` sitting in the SUCCESS payload, with zero language diagnostics and zero emitted-TypeScript diagnostics. The array-literal spelling of the same value edge. The callee reads `handlers[0]` and invokes it, which is the identical boundary crossing as a direct argument.
